reason: Both conversations open with the same correct emergency response (stop, no switches or flames, isolate at the meter, ventilate, leave, call 0800 111 999). Conversation 1 then handles the homeowner's panicked follow-up well: it treats the headache as possible exposure, reinforces leaving the property, directs them to call from outside and to report symptoms, and keeps them away from any investigation or relighting. Conversation 2 ends after the first turn, so it never engages with the meter question, the headache, the rented-property situation or the no-CO-alarm detail, and offers no reassurance to a panicking person. Neither recommends a part, which is correct; conversation 1 could have added 'tell the landlord and get a Gas Safe engineer before any use', but it still served the homeowner more completely.
